text: The operation, the payload and the element names of the checked-fields read come from RWB-P5-E2025-CON and are never guessed; the treatment columns that carry the facts are named for the extracted codes (contract_amount, contract_date, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office, title_doc_no) with source_document_id, source_doc_version and source_table_version beside them, and the amounts and dates follow the numeric(18,2) and date conventions TSD S2 T3.1 already uses for DF-TRT-007, DF-TRT-008 and DF-TRT-031; the type-table version stamped on the row is the tableVersion of the reader's answer the facts were written from; a field code with no treatment column of the same name is not mapped; and the masking of party_names is the hub's, this service storing no party name at all.
why: No source names the read across the service boundary, gives the treatment a contract or mortgage column, says which service stamps the type-table version, or settles the masking rule on this side, while R-UNI-38 and CTL-08 require the version in force with the value; leaving them blank would make the story unbuildable and inventing a business value would be worse.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 4, 11, 12, 13 and 19; TSD S2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S2 A2.1.3.1 (BR-S2-001); Architecture v5 slide 8; context pack S2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11
confirm: The rwb-document contract owner publishes the operation, the payload and the masking rule, and the rwb-treatment data owner approves the fact columns in the DDL, at the wave 2 contract freeze
impact: Medium: a change in the column set or the masking rule is one migration and one criterion, and no rewrite of the story.

text: This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-025: the classification, the extraction, the evaluation runner, the review queue and the eleven legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC11 stay with RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the shapes, the path, the state filter and the fakes of the reader are RWB-P5-E2025-CON's, and the two requirements of the plan's list that the legacy key puts out of scope (REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018) are answered by the document hub and tested by no criterion here. This story writes eight criteria of its own.
why: One legacy capability cannot have two owners of the same criteria; the work package carries the key as Split (rework) with an empty acs list for this story, and the same eleven criteria cannot be owned by P5, S2 and S4 at once.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 1 to 19, its section 7 acceptance criteria and its section 19 out-of-scope list; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7; work package B2-S2-021 story line for RWB-S2-E2025-APP
applied_in: Sections 1, 7 and 16; the requirement rows of section 18; fragment acs and reqs
confirm: The P5 slice owner confirms that RWB-P5-E2025-APP carries the eleven legacy criteria word for word with their origin tags
impact: Low: the split follows the ownership map and the work package.

text: No personal data is written, logged or put on an event by this story: the row, the log lines, the workflow input and any payload carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the document ID and version, the type-table version, field codes, amounts and dates only. party_names is masked by the hub, is never mapped onto a column, and a property test fails the build if a party name reaches a row, a log line or a span attribute.
why: The guardrail of Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17 and the legacy guardrail forbid personal data in events, workflow inputs and logs, and the legacy authority note grants unmasked values to SY-CASEWF and SY-AGENT only, so this service must hold none.
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 12, 17 and BR7; CTL-11 and DL26
confirm: The privacy owner confirms the field set of the treatment read and of any payload the stage handles
impact: Low: the payload is narrower than the sources allow.

text: The outbox and inbox library, the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the workflow kit and the gateway-bff composite route are platform wave-0 and shared-library deliverables the service template already carries: they stand in no build row of this story, the metadata keeps Depends on (build) None and Contract dependencies RWB-P5-E2025-CON only, and the story builds against their fakes until they publish.
why: The pattern table adds five H rows and two C rows for DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19 while the work package's build list is empty and its only contract is the P5 one; every added row is a platform library or a contract the template or another service already publishes, and inventing H rows would change the build sequence of the lane.

text: This slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and both rows stay in the pattern list as prohibitions. DP-09 is used only through the outbox and inbox library for the idempotency and inbox tables of rwb_treatment and the one write key of the apply: the hub's extraction event is rwb-document's and this service carries no integration dependency on it, and the one event of rwb-treatment, TreatmentApproved, belongs to the approval story. DP-10 registers nothing: the intake job JOB-12 and the retention run JOB-17 are rwb-document's, and the stage clock the activity runs under is the parent workflow's.
why: Declaring a producer for an event no source assigns would put an outbox row into a slice that owns no event, and declaring a Schedule would add a job no source places in this capability; carrying both as prohibitions keeps the pattern list intact and makes the reading visible.
read: TSD S2 T5.3 (TreatmentApproved published); context pack S2 (one event, EV-10; one workflow, TreatmentWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and DP-10; legacy RWB-E2-025 sections 4, 12 and 13
applied_in: Sections 1, 3, 12.3, 12.4, 12.6, 13 and 17; fragment events_published and events_consumed
confirm: The event catalogue owner confirms that no event and no Schedule is assigned to the treatment-side document-fact fill
impact: Low: no event and no Schedule means no catalogue change and no chart change.

text: The checked-fields read is consumed as one REST hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker against the contract and its fake, as DP-11 and the work package give it, and not as a Temporal activity on queue rwb-document as the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 would have it; the payload, the state filter and the criteria are the same under either transport, so a later decision to move the call to Temporal changes the client and the fake and no criterion.
why: The architecture catalogue outranks the pattern table under R3, but the P5 contract publishes no checked-field activity, so following the matrix would leave nothing to build against on Day 1 while the legacy interface and DP-11 both describe a call that returns a value within the request.
